# BeautifulSoup

HTML/XML parsing library, used in labs 10 and 11 of [[python-programming-laboratories]] for scraping
and for a document pipeline that extracts 41 chapters of text.

## Defensive scraping, because the target moved

The lab README records the situation plainly: *"The faculty site has been restructured since the
exercise was set."* The scraper was written to survive that rather than to match one snapshot — the
parsing is tolerant of structure it does not recognise instead of indexing blindly into a fixed tree.

Paired with `requests`, the network side is equally defensive: a `timeout=` on **every** request, and
`raise_for_status()` **before** anything is written to disk, so a 404 error page is never saved as if
it were the content. Both are the kind of guard that only gets written after it has bitten someone —
see [[document-the-failure-mode-next-to-the-fix]].

The REST client in the same lab accepts both a bare list and a `{"data": …}` envelope, because
tolerating two response shapes is cheaper than pinning an API you do not control.

**TODO:** what the original scraper targeted, and whether the lab was reworked or merely patched when
the site changed, is not recorded. `confidence: low` on the history.

## The 4.13 API removal

> "**Two library APIs moved.** `Image.ANTIALIAS` and `ImageDraw.textsize` were removed in Pillow 10;
> `findAll(text=True)` was removed in BeautifulSoup 4.13."
> — Python-Programming-Laboratories/labs/11_report_pipeline/README.md, 2026-07-25

`findAll(text=True)` was the long-deprecated camelCase alias with the old keyword; the modern form is
`find_all(string=True)`. The port is one line and the diagnosis is the expensive part, which is why
it is written down beside the code rather than left in a commit message — none of these commits
exist, see [[import-finished-work-into-git]]. The [[pillow]] half of the same note is recorded there.

`labs/04_classes/requests.py` shadows the `requests` package that this lab and lab 11 import, if that
directory ever ends up on `sys.path`. `confidence: high` — see
[[python-programming-laboratories]].
